The position requires strong contract drafting and analytical skills, independent judgment, transaction-management experience, and the ability to identify legal, commercial, financing, and execution risks while coordinating efficiently with internal stakeholders, outside counsel, lenders, investors, customers, vendors, consultants, landowners, and other counterparties. Manage closing checklists and monitor financing conditions precedent, outstanding diligence requirements, post-closing obligations, and project-specific exceptions. Coordinate with lenders, investors, outside counsel, independent engineers, insurance consultants, appraisal firms, and internal finance teams. Assist with the preparation, collection, review, organization, and delivery of transaction documents for financing closings. Review project agreements and supporting documentation to identify inconsistencies, missing documents, consent requirements, contractual restrictions, and financing risks. Evaluate contractual requirements against project development, engineering, construction, operational, and financing assumptions. Work cross-functionally to develop practical solutions to diligence findings and closing conditions. Support formation and governance documentation, LLC agreements, resolutions, written consents, officer certificates, organizational records, and authorization packages. Coordinate execution of corporate approvals and transaction documents through electronic-signature platforms. Standaardiseren van observability voor metrics, logs en traces. Ontwikkelen van selfservice en begeleiden van teams bij adoptie. Unieke pipelines, handmatige configuraties en deploymentfouten nemen af, terwijl het gebruik van platformstandaarden groeit. review_candidates.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. We are looking for an experienced Optomechanical Engineer to contribute to the development of advanced optical instruments and space-qualified telescope systems. In this role, you will take ownership of optomechanical design activities, from initial concepts and detailed engineering through alignment, integration, and environmental qualification. You will work on sophisticated optical assemblies, including large mirrors and lenses of up to 600 mm in diameter, ensuring precision, reliability, and performance under demanding space conditions. Collaborating with multidisciplinary engineering teams, you will combine mechanical design, optical analysis, and hands-on laboratory expertise to deliver mission-critical hardware. You will also contribute to improving engineering methodologies, manufacturing processes, and product reliability. This is an opportunity to work on cutting-edge aerospace technology within an international, collaborative environment, with significant potential for professional growth and increased technical responsibility. Accountabilities Lead the conceptual and detailed optomechanical design of space telescopes and optical instruments, including mirrors, lenses, windows, filters, and focal plane interfaces. Design precision optical mounts, including kinematic, semi-kinematic, flexure-based, and bonded mounting solutions, while minimizing stress and optical distortion. Develop low-distortion flexures, bipods, telescope support structures, metering structures, and manual or motorized focus mechanisms using athermal design principles. Select appropriate materials and adhesives for precision space optics, considering thermal expansion, dimensional stability, mechanical properties, and space qualification requirements. Perform structural and thermal finite element analyses (FEA), including modal, quasi-static, random vibration, and thermo-elastic analyses, while supporting integrated Structural-Thermal-Optical Performance (STOP) assessments. Define and conduct optomechanical tolerance analyses and error budgets, evaluating decenter, tilt, despace, surface figure, and mechanical stability in collaboration with optical designers. Develop alignment and integration strategies and participate directly in laboratory activities, including optical alignment, metrology, and environmental qualification testing. Support vibration and thermal vacuum test campaigns, correlate experimental results with analytical models, and ensure optical performance throughout qualification. Prepare detailed engineering drawings and technical specifications using Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) and ISO 10110 optical drawing standards. Act as a technical point of contact for optics and precision-mechanics suppliers, supporting component specifications, manufacturing, and quality requirements. Produce technical documentation, analysis reports, and engineering deliverables while maintaining accurate optomechanical information within CAD and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems. Collaborate closely with mechanical design, structural, and thermal engineering teams to ensure system-level integration, manufacturability, and compliance with mission requirements. Contribute to the continuous improvement of optomechanical design practices, product reliability, and engineering processes. Requirements Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aeronautical Engineering, Optical Engineering, Physics, or a related discipline, ideally with a specialization in optomechanics or precision engineering. Between 3 and 6 years of professional experience as an Optomechanical Engineer within the aerospace sector. Demonstrated involvement in at least one space or airborne optical instrument project, such as a telescope, camera, spectrometer, radiometer, or LiDAR system, preferably covering the full development cycle through qualification testing. Proven experience designing optical mounts for lenses and mirrors, as well as telescope support structures. Practical experience with finite element analysis of optical systems and environmental testing campaigns, particularly vibration and thermal vacuum testing. Advanced understanding of optomechanical engineering principles, including kinematic mounting, flexure design, athermalization, optical bonding, and mount-induced stress control. Proficiency in 3D CAD software, preferably Siemens NX, and FEA tools using NASTRAN-compatible solvers. Ability to perform STOP analyses, including Zernike polynomial fitting of FEA surface deformations and rigid-body motions, using tools such as SigFit or equivalent in-house solutions. Strong knowledge of precision engineering materials, including Zerodur, ULE, silicon carbide, aluminum, titanium, Invar, and carbon-fiber-reinforced polymers (CFRP), as well as space-qualified adhesives. Expertise in GD&T and optical engineering drawing standards, particularly ISO 10110. Hands-on experience with optical alignment and metrology equipment, such as interferometers, autocollimators, coordinate measuring machines (CMM), and alignment telescopes. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, excellent attention to detail, and the capacity to translate complex engineering challenges into practical solutions. Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary and international teams. Advanced English proficiency, both written and spoken. Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to offices, laboratories, suppliers, and other project locations, including laboratory activities in Uruguay. Candidates must be eligible to work on projects subject to applicable ITAR export control restrictions; U.S. persons are not eligible for this position. Additional Qualifications Considered An Advantage Experience designing and testing large optical systems, particularly mirrors and telescopes of up to 600 mm in diameter. Knowledge of lightweight mirror structures, gravity sag, and 1-g offloading techniques during optical alignment and testing. Experience with reflective telescope architectures, including Cassegrain, Ritchey-Chrétien, Korsch, and Three-Mirror Anastigmat configurations. Experience correlating STOP predictions with interferometric measurements on space telescope systems. Familiarity with Zemax OpticStudio and Siemens Simcenter 3D for FEA pre-processing and post-processing. Specialized training in optomechanical design, tolerancing, integrated optomechanical analysis, optical FEA, or adhesive bonding of optical elements. Technical publications, conference presentations, particularly through SPIE, or patents related to optomechanics. Knowledge of ECSS and NASA engineering standards, as well as cleanliness and contamination control requirements for space optics. Previous experience in NewSpace or small-satellite environments, particularly with design-for-manufacturing principles and production scalability.
